newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian war veterans protest over their plight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian war veterans protest over their plight.

text.p: Several thousand Croatian war veterans, many invalids in wheelchairs and on crutches, staged a city centre protest in Zagreb on Sunday, accusing authorities of neglecting their plight.
Some 4,000 demonstrators who gathered in front of the parliament building said the government had failed to provide job opportunities, apartments and post-war rehabilitation programmes.
"In 1991 we knew what we wanted...But now we know it too -- we want to live in a legal state," head of the Croatian Association of Disabled Vetarans (HVIDRA) Marinko Liovic told a crowd.
Croatia in 1991 fought a war against minority Serbs who rebelled against the country's secession from Yugoslavia and seized one third of Croatian territory.
After a four-year-long ceasefire, Croatia recaptured most breakway Serb enclaves in offensives in the summer of 1995.
According to the Defence Ministry, more than 150,000 soldiers have been demobilised since 1992. HVIDRA says it has almost 20,000 registered members.
President Franjo Tudjman said on Saturday that the government planned to allocate 1.2 billion kuna ($225 million) for invalids' needs, the state news agency HINA reported.
Defence Minister Gojko Susak, who was present at the rally, said he would see to it that Tudjman kept his promise.

"It was easier in 1991 when we knew who we were fighting against," a veteran who requested anonymity told Reuters. "They tell me now - nobody pushed you to fight...Once you mattered, now you matter no more."
